context: Algebra: nonempty semigroup with two-sided identity, no inverses required
editorial_note: Direct ProofWiki monoid axioms S0–S2 read: closure, associativity and identity. This notion does not require inverses or commutativity.
potential_contextual_variants: associative operation and identity as data
text: A monoid is a nonempty set M equipped with an associative binary operation M×M→M and an element e∈M such that e⋆x=x=x⋆e for every x∈M.

context: Set algebra: mapping of two inputs versus internal operation closed on a carrier
editorial_note: The ProofWiki source explicitly contrasts its general two-input mapping definition with the frequently used alternative where codomain equals carrier. These are not automatically the same type.
text: A binary operation with input sets S,T and outputs in U is a function ⋆:S×T→U. For an internal binary operation on S the type is ⋆:S×S→S, making closure on S part of the signature.

context: Set theory: relation as S,T,R triple or truth-set R⊆S×T
editorial_note: Direct ProofWiki primary definition treats S,T as part of the relation; the separately labeled 'also defined as' treatment identifies only the subset. Two equivalent usage contexts need not represent identical objects.
potential_contextual_variants: subset R of Cartesian product with carrier context
text: A binary relation from S to T may be represented by a triple (S,T,R) where R⊆S×T; in an alternative common treatment, the relation is identified with the subset R⊆S×T itself. A relation on S uses T=S.

context: Set theory: binary Cartesian product of sets and ordered pairs
editorial_note: Direct ProofWiki binary set-product definition read. Keep finite, indexed and infinite products as distinct formulations/contexts rather than conflating them with binary S×T.
text: For sets S and T, the Cartesian product S×T is the set of ordered pairs (s,t) such that s∈S and t∈T.
